title: To the Father's Love We Trust
description: To the Father's Love We Trust in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 412, “Funeral Hymn of a Child”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: To the Fa-ther's love we trust That which was en-shrined in dust; While we give the earth to earth, Finds the soul its heav-enly birth. An-gels wait the an-gel child, Gen-tle, young, and un-de-filed.

lines: To the Father's love we trust
That which was enshrined in dust;
While we give the earth to earth,
Finds the soul its heavenly birth.
Said not oft those pleading eyes
That they longed for purer skies?
Did not oft the falling tear
Prayed we not that she might rest
Give the spirit, then, to God,
And its vesture to the sod;
Life, henceforth, shall have a ray
And a light from angel eyes
Draw us upward to the skies.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
